A California-based Apple user has filed a lawsuit proposing a class action, accusing the company of misleading consumers about the privacy protections of its "Hide My Email" feature. Here are the details of the case.

Apple sued over alleged flaw in 'Hide My Email' feature

Recently, 404 Media reported that Apple had been aware of a vulnerability in its "Hide My Email" feature for over a year, one that could potentially expose the real email address hidden behind an alias.

Apple's "Hide My Email" feature allows users to create unique, randomly generated email addresses that forward messages to their personal inbox, so they don't have to disclose their real email address when signing up for apps, websites, or newsletter subscriptions.

The feature is available for free through "Sign in with Apple," while a more comprehensive version is included in the iCloud+ plan starting at $0.99 per month, allowing users to create aliases for websites, newsletters, and other services.

According to 404 Media, a security researcher alerted Apple in June 2025 that a vulnerability could potentially expose the real email address behind a "Hide My Email" alias.

Apple reportedly confirmed receiving the report about a month later but allegedly did not address the issue. In March 2026, the company stated that it had patched the vulnerability, but the researcher found that it could still be exploited.

Back to the main point. According to MacRumors, plaintiff Anthony Alvarez stated:

Apple has long been aware of the issue for over a year, yet the vulnerability remains unfixed—during which time Apple has continued to profit from "Hide My Email" and its privacy promises. The plaintiff is one of millions of customers who pay for iCloud+ and trust Apple's claim that "Hide My Email" will protect their personal email address. Both the plaintiff and the class members have paid Apple for privacy—iCloud+ subscribers through a premium baked into their iCloud+ subscription fees, and all Apple customers through the price premium of Apple products that include privacy protections and features like "Hide My Email."

The lawsuit also claims this is not an isolated incident, citing a 2023 report indicating that Apple's random MAC address feature may expose users' real hardware identifiers.

The complaint also states that the total damages claimed by the proposed class members exceed $5 million (excluding interest and litigation costs), though it does not explain how that figure was calculated.

Alvarez filed the lawsuit on behalf of himself and other Apple customers who claim to have been similarly affected. He is asking the court to certify the case as a class action, covering four proposed user groups:

  • A nationwide group of Apple customers who purchased devices and used "Hide My Email";
  • A California subgroup of the aforementioned users;
  • A nationwide subgroup of iCloud+ subscribers who have used the feature;
  • A California subgroup of iCloud+ subscribers.

He is demanding a jury trial and, in addition to monetary damages in an amount to be determined, is asking the court to order Apple to fix the "Hide My Email" feature or clearly disclose its limitations.

Apple has yet to respond to the lawsuit.

Do you think this class action should be certified? Let us know in the comments.
